learning_outcomes.text: Using graphic principles and tools for describing and designing mechanical systems and processes.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Object and place of machine elements in the training of mechanical engineers
Basic principles of design in the construction of machines, equipment, installations, and facilities.
Friction wheel transmissions; Belt transmissions; Mechanical variators;
Gear transmissions (form). Gears (toothed wheels); Reducers, gearboxes and feed; Chain and synchronous belt transmissions
Design of a narrow/wide multi-layer V-belt drive - initial data
Calculation of geometric parameters of belt transmissions
Selection and calculation of pitch diameters
Selection of belt type. Belt parameter calculation
Belt parameter calculation, Kinematic, kinetostatic analysis, dimensioning and verification of belt pulleys
Belt drawing - cross-section, dimensioning and verification of the belt. Friction coefficient
Kinetostatic calculation, verification for allowable stresses
teaching_methods: Laboratory work (using functional stands and laboratory guides)
assessment_rules: The written exam assesses the assimilation of fundamental theoretical knowledge (66%). Laboratory activities are evaluated based on performance, with objective evidence provided by how activities are organized and conducted, and prompt feedback (33%). The minimum performance standard for passing requires knowledge of the operation, calculation, selection, and design of a machine element presented in the course.
